To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the risk of breast cancer is associated with a combination of long duration of ovulation (a marker of ovarian activity) and mild hypothyroid states.
women combining long duration of ovulation with low levels of circulating thyroid hormones may be at increased breast cancer risk.
women combining low free T4 levels with long duration of menstrual cycle are at increased risk for breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the thyroid in the etiology and pathogenesis of breast cancer.
the role of thyroid hormones in the pathogenesis of breast cancer, and the potential interaction between these hormones and ovarian steroids.
the hypothesis that thyroid and ovarian hormones interact in the etiology and prevention of breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the association between mild thyroid dysfunction and breast cancer is weak and that the association is likely due to confounding factors.
thyroid hormones may be involved in the etiology, pathogenesis, and/or clinical course of breast cancer.
the relationship between thyroid function and breast cancer remains unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thyroid hormones and duration of ovarian activity may be important factors in the etiology and/or prognosis of breast cancer.
the combination of a long duration of ovulation and low levels of circulating T4 may contribute to the etiology of human breast cancer.
thyroid hormones may have a role in the etiology and progression of breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thyroid hormone levels and duration of ovulation should be considered together in the evaluation of the etiologic role of thyroid hormones in the development of breast cancer.
the thyroid and ovary are not isolated systems and that their interactions should be considered in the etiology and treatment of breast cancer.
thyroid and ovarian hormones may act together to influence the risk of breast cancer.
